questions.title: GATE CSE 1996 | Question: 1.5
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Two dice are thrown simultaneously. The probability that at least one of them will have $6$ facing up is

  1. $\frac{1}{36}$

  2. $\frac{1}{3}$

  3. $\frac{25}{36}$

  4. $\frac{11}{36}$

review.independentCheck: Complement count: neither die shows 6 with probability (5/6)^2, so the requested probability is 11/36.
review.notes: Complement count: neither die shows 6 with probability (5/6)^2, so the requested probability is 11/36.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1996 | Question: 1.6
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
The formula used to compute an approximation for the second derivative of a function $f$ at a point $X_0$ is

  1. $\dfrac{f(x_0 +h) + f(x_0 – h)}{2}$

  2. $\dfrac{f(x_0 +h) - f(x_0 – h)}{2h}$

  3. $\dfrac{f(x_0 +h) + 2f(x_0) + f(x_0 – h)}{h^2}$ 

  4. $\dfrac{f(x_0 +h) - 2f(x_0) + f(x_0 – h)}{h^2}$

review.independentCheck: Central Taylor differences cancel the first derivative and isolate f''(x0), yielding option D.
review.notes: Central Taylor differences cancel the first derivative and isolate f''(x0), yielding option D.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1996 | Question: 1.7
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Let $Ax = b$ be a system of linear equations where $A$ is an $m \times n$ matrix and $b$ is a $m \times 1$ column vector and $X$ is an $n \times1$ column vector of unknowns. Which of the following is false?

  1. The system has a solution if and only if, both $A$ and the augmented matrix $[Ab]$ have the same rank.

  2. If $m < n$ and $b$ is the zero vector, then the system has infinitely many solutions.

  3. If $m=n$ and $b$ is a non-zero vector, then the system has a unique solution.

  4. The system will have only a trivial solution when $m=n$, $b$ is the zero vector and $\text{rank}(A) =n$.

review.independentCheck: A square system with nonzero b need not be nonsingular or uniquely solvable; option C is false.
review.notes: A square system with nonzero b need not be nonsingular or uniquely solvable; option C is false.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1996 | Question: 2.1
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Let $R$ denote the set of real numbers. Let $f:R\times R \rightarrow R \times R$ be a bijective function defined by $f(x,y) = (x+y, x-y)$. The inverse function of $f$ is given by

  1. $f^{-1} (x,y) = \left( \frac {1}{x+y}, \frac{1}{x-y}\right)$

  2. $f^{ -1} (x,y) = (x-y , x+y)$

  3. $f^{-1} (x,y) = \left( \frac {x+y}{2}, \frac{x-y}{2}\right)$

  4. $f^{-1}(x,y)=\left [ 2\left(x-y\right),2\left(x+y\right) \right ]$

review.independentCheck: Solve u=x+y and v=x-y for x,y to obtain the inverse in option C.
review.notes: Solve u=x+y and v=x-y for x,y to obtain the inverse in option C.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1996 | Question: 2.2
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Let $R$ be a non-empty relation on a collection of sets defined by $_{A}R_ B$ if and only if $A \cap B = \phi$. Then, (pick the true statement)

  1. $A$ is reflexive and transitive

  2. $R$ is symmetric and not transitive

  3. $R$ is an equivalence relation

  4. $R$ is not reflexive and not symmetric

review.independentCheck: Disjointness is symmetric; {1},{2},{1} is a counterexample to transitivity.
review.notes: Disjointness is symmetric; {1},{2},{1} is a counterexample to transitivity.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1996 | Question: 2.3
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following is NOT True?

(Read $\wedge$ as AND, $\vee$ as OR, $\neg$ as NOT,  $\rightarrow$ as one way implication and $\leftrightarrow$ as two way implication)

  1. $((x \rightarrow y) \wedge x) \rightarrow y$

  2. $((\neg x \rightarrow y) \wedge (\neg x \rightarrow \neg y)) \rightarrow x$

  3. $(x \rightarrow (x \vee y))$

  4. $((x \vee y) \leftrightarrow (\neg x \rightarrow \neg y))$

review.independentCheck: A, B, and C are tautologies; x=false,y=true makes the biconditional in D false.
review.notes: A, B, and C are tautologies; x=false,y=true makes the biconditional in D false.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1996 | Question: 2.4
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Which one of the following is false?

  1. The set of all bijective functions on a finite set forms a group under function composition
  2. The set $\{1, 2, \dots p-1\}$ forms a group under multiplication mod $p$, where $p$ is a prime number
  3. The set of all strings over a finite alphabet forms a group under concatenation
  4. A subset $S \neq \emptyset$ of $G$ is a subgroup of the group $\langle G, * \rangle$ if and only if for any pair of elements $a, b \in S, a * b^{-1} \in S$

review.independentCheck: Nonempty strings lack concatenation inverses, so the set of all strings is not a group.
review.notes: Nonempty strings lack concatenation inverses, so the set of all strings is not a group.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1996 | Question: 2.6
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
The matrices $\begin{bmatrix} \cos\theta && -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta && \cos\theta \end{bmatrix}$ and $\begin{bmatrix} a && 0\\ 0&& b \end{bmatrix}$ commute under multiplication

  1. if $a=b \text{ or } \theta = n\pi, n$ an integer
  2. always
  3. never
  4. if $a \cos\theta = b \sin\theta$

review.independentCheck: The two products commute exactly when (a-b)sin(theta)=0.
review.notes: The two products commute exactly when (a-b)sin(theta)=0.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1996 | Question: 2.7
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
The probability that top and bottom cards of a randomly shuffled deck are both aces is

  1. $\frac{4}{52} \times \frac{4}{52}$

  2. $\frac{4}{52} \times \frac{3}{52}$

  3. $\frac{4}{52} \times \frac{3}{51}$

  4. $\frac{4}{52} \times \frac{4}{51}$

review.independentCheck: After drawing one ace, 3 of 51 cards remain aces; the answer is 4/52 times 3/51.
review.notes: After drawing one ace, 3 of 51 cards remain aces; the answer is 4/52 times 3/51.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 1.19
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Let $R$ be a symmetric and transitive relation on a set $A$. Then

  1. $R$ is reflexive and hence an equivalence relation
  2. $R$ is reflexive and hence a partial order
  3. $R$ is reflexive and hence not an equivalence relation
  4. None of the above

review.independentCheck: The empty relation on a nonempty set is symmetric and transitive but not reflexive, so none of A-C follows.
review.notes: The empty relation on a nonempty set is symmetric and transitive but not reflexive, so none of A-C follows.

questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
The number of elements in the power set $P(S)$ of the set $S=\{\{\emptyset\}, 1, \{2, 3\}\}$ is:

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 1.22
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics

If at every point of a certain curve, the slope of the tangent equals [latex]\frac{-2x}{y}[/latex] the curve is

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 1.24
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
The rank of the following $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix, where $a$ is a real number is $$ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & a & a^2 & \dots & a^n  \\ 1 & a & a^2 & \dots & a^n \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \: & \vdots \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \: & \vdots \\ 1 & a & a^2 & \dots & a^n \end{bmatrix}$$

  1. $1$
  2. $2$
  3. $n$
  4. Depends on the value of $a$

review.independentCheck: All rows equal a nonzero vector whose first coordinate is 1; rank is exactly one.
review.notes: All rows equal a nonzero vector whose first coordinate is 1; rank is exactly one.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 2.8
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
If the cube roots of unity are $1, \omega$ and $\omega^2$, then the roots of the following equation are $$(x-1)^3 +8 =0$$

  1. $-1, 1 + 2\omega, 1 + 2\omega^2$   
  2. $1, 1 - 2\omega, 1 - 2\omega^2$
  3. $-1, 1 - 2\omega, 1 - 2\omega^2$
  4. $-1, 1 + 2\omega, -1 + 2\omega^2$

review.independentCheck: The roots of (x-1)^3=-8 are -1, 1-2omega, and 1-2omega^2.

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
A unit vector perpendicular to both the vectors $a=2i-3j+k$ and $b=i+j-2k$ is:

  1. $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} (i+j+k)$

  4. $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} (i+j-k)$

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 2.17
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Let $A$ be the set of all non-singular matrices over real number and let $*$ be the matrix multiplication operation. Then

  1. $A$ is closed under $*$ but $\langle A, *\rangle$ is not a semigroup.
  2. $\langle A, *\rangle$ is a semigroup but not a monoid.
  3. $\langle A, * \rangle$ is a monoid but not a group.
  4. $\langle A, *\rangle$ is a a group but not an abelian group.

review.independentCheck: GL_n(R) is a group and is nonabelian for n>=2; explicit 2x2 matrices do not commute.
review.notes: GL_n(R) is a group and is nonabelian for n>=2; explicit 2x2 matrices do not commute.
